about: What an HSA, health FSA or dependent care FSA can pay for, by purchase category. IRS rules, the same for everyone; a plan can be narrower, never wider.

medical.note: Prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and menstrual care products qualify. Toiletries, cosmetics and general-health vitamins don't.
medical.source_excerpt: In addition, over-the-counter products and medications are now reimbursable without a prescription. ... the cost of menstrual care products is now reimbursable. The new rules apply to amounts paid after Dec. 31, 2019.

medical.note: Care to diagnose, treat or prevent a condition (visits, copays, tests, procedures). Cosmetic surgery doesn't qualify.
medical.source_excerpt: Medical expenses are the costs of diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease

medical.note: Cleanings, fillings, braces and other dental care qualify. Whitening doesn't.
medical.source_excerpt: You can include in medical expenses the amounts you pay for the prevention and alleviation of dental disease. ... You can't include in medical expenses amounts paid to whiten teeth.

medical.note: Glasses and contact lenses needed for medical reasons qualify.
medical.source_excerpt: You can include in medical expenses amounts you pay for eyeglasses and contact lenses needed for medical reasons.

medical.note: Gym and health club dues don't qualify. Separate fees for a weight-loss program that treats a specific disease can, usually with a doctor's letter.
medical.source_excerpt: You can't include membership dues in a gym, health club, or spa as medical expenses ... but you can include separate fees charged there for weight loss activities

medical.note: Childcare isn't a medical expense. A dependent care FSA covers it instead.
medical.source_excerpt: You can't include in medical expenses amounts you pay for the care of children, even if the expenses enable you

dependent_care.note: Care for a child under 13 (daycare, after-school care) so you can work.
dependent_care.source_excerpt: Pre-tax contributions you made under a dependent care flexible spending arrangement. ... A qualifying person is: Your qualifying child who is your dependent and who was under age 13 when the care was provided
